question: At approximately what ambient temperature (~25–30°C) does rigor mortis typically begin, reach full development, and resolve?

answers.text: Begins 30 min after death; full rigor in 2 hours; resolves in 6–8 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These timings are too rapid. At 25–30°C, rigor starts later and lasts considerably longer.

answers.text: Begins 1–2 hours after death; full rigor in 6–12 hours; resolves in 24–36 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. At approximately 25–30°C: onset 1–2 hours, full development 6–12 hours, resolution (secondary flaccidity) 24–36 hours. These timings vary significantly with ambient temperature — cold slows and delays rigor; heat accelerates it.

answers.text: Begins 4–6 hours after death; full rigor in 12–24 hours; resolves in 48–72 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These timings reflect colder conditions. At 25–30°C, rigor develops faster than this.

answers.text: Rigor mortis timing is fixed and does not vary with ambient temperature

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Temperature is the most important modifier of rigor mortis timing. Hot environments accelerate both onset and resolution; cold environments delay both. PMI estimates based on rigor alone must always include a temperature caveat.

overallFeedback.feedback: At ~25–30°C: rigor begins 1–2 hours after death, reaches full rigidity in 6–12 hours, and resolves (secondary flaccidity) in 24–36 hours. Temperature is the single most important modifier — always include it in PMI estimates.
